task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

The payment went through and your line is now **Active** again.

Here's what I confirmed:
- Bill **B1234321** for **$65.00** — status: **Paid**
- Line **555-123-2002** — status: **Active** (suspension lifted)

**One important step for you:** please restart (reboot) your phone. Your device needs to reboot to reconnect to the network and pick up the restored service. After it powers back on, the "No Service" message should clear and you should see your signal bars return.

Other than that, there's nothing else you need to do. Is there anything else I can help with?
turns.execution_output: User: Oh, a restart? That makes me nervous — I have photos of my grandchildren on this phone that I'd be absolutely heartbroken to lose. Will restarting it erase any of those? I've never really done this before...

turns.thought:
No need to worry at all — restarting your phone is completely safe and will not erase anything. It doesn't delete photos, contacts, messages, or any of your apps. Think of it like turning a light switch off and back on: everything is still exactly where you left it when it comes back on. Those precious photos of your grandchildren will be right there waiting for you.

Here's how to do it, nice and easy:

1. **Press and hold the power button** on the side of your phone (for most phones, it's on the right side).
2. Hold it down until a menu appears on the screen — usually after a few seconds.
3. Tap **"Restart"** (or **"Reboot"**). If you see **"Power off"** instead, tap that instead.

(If you only get "Power off": once the screen goes completely black and the phone is off, press and hold the power button again until you see the manufacturer's logo, then let go.)

4. Wait about 30–60 seconds for it to finish starting back up.
5. Once it's back on, check the top of your screen — the "No Service" message should be gone and your signal bars should have returned.

As long as your phone has at least a little bit of battery (above 5%), it will start back up fine. You won't lose a thing.

Would you like me to wait here while you try it? I'm happy to stay with you until you see those bars come back.

turns.thought:
Good news — that's actually very encouraging! You're absolutely right, and your instinct is spot on.

**Yes, that little airplane symbol is the problem.** It means "Airplane Mode" is turned on. When it's on, your phone deliberately switches off all of its wireless connections — that's why there are no signal bars. It's a setting, not a fault, and it's very easy to turn off. It's likely it got switched on by accident.

Also, the fact that "No Service" is gone and the airplane icon has appeared is a good sign — it means your line itself is fine. We just need to switch that setting off.

Here's how to turn it off:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of the screen** with one finger. This opens your "Quick Settings" panel — a little menu with round or square buttons.
2. Look for the button with the **airplane symbol** on it. It's currently lit up or highlighted (often blue or white) because it's ON.
3. **Tap that airplane button once.** It should go dim or grey, and the airplane symbol at the top of your screen should disappear.
4. Wait about **10–30 seconds**. Your signal bars should come back, and you may see "5G", "LTE", or "4G" appear next to them.

If you don't see the airplane button right away, swipe down once more from the top to expand the full list of buttons — it's usually near the top alongside Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

Nothing will be erased by doing this, and it's perfectly safe.

Give that a try and tell me what you see at the top of your screen afterward. I'll stay right here with you until this is sorted out.

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data back on:**

1. Swipe down from the top of the screen again, same as you did before.
2. Look for a button with a **little up-and-down arrow** or two arrows (often labeled "Mobile Data" or "Cellular Data"). It's currently greyed out or dim because it's off.
3. **Tap it once** so it lights up.
4. Wait about **30 seconds** and see if any bars appear.

If you don't spot it, swipe down a second time to see the full list of buttons.

Now, the "No Signal" part may take a little more work after that. There are two more common causes we can try, and I'll walk you through them one at a time so it stays simple. We won't need to do anything risky — no erasing, no complicated menus.

turns.thought:
Please don't apologize, and take a breath — you have not made anything worse, and you definitely haven't broken anything. That message is just a bit confusingly worded; it's simply telling you what the setting is *right now*. Mobile data being off isn't harmful at all — it only affects internet use while you're away from Wi-Fi. It does not affect your ability to make calls. So nothing is damaged.

And here's the reassuring part: your account is in perfect order on my end. Your line 555-123-2002 is **Active**, your bill is **Paid**, and your device (Smartphone Pro Max) shows as properly activated. So the remaining problem is purely a setting or connection on the phone itself, which is very fixable.

The most important thing to focus on now is the **"No Signal"** part, not the data.

Let's try one simple thing that very often solves exactly this:

**Restart your phone once more.** And you already know how to do this safely — you did it beautifully last time, and none of your photos went anywhere.

1. Press and hold the **power button** on the side.
2. Tap **"Restart"** (or "Power off," then hold the button again to turn it back on).
3. Wait a full **60 seconds** after it comes back on.

The reason this helps: after being in Airplane Mode, the phone sometimes needs a fresh start to go out and reconnect to the network properly. Now that Airplane Mode is off, this second restart should let it find the signal.

While you wait the 60 seconds, if it's easy for you, try standing near a window or moving to a different room — being indoors away from windows can sometimes weaken signal.

Is there any chance you happen to know a family member, neighbour, or friend who could sit with you for this next step? Not because you're doing anything wrong — you're doing really well — but just so you've got a second pair of eyes and someone there with you.

Try that restart and tell me what the top of the screen says afterward. I'm staying right here with you. And if this doesn't bring the bars back, I'll arrange for you to speak with a technical specialist who can dig deeper with you — so you're not on your own either way.
